newsitem.title: USA: Centennial sees likely reason for trade rise.
newsitem.headline: Centennial sees likely reason for trade rise.

text.p: Centennial Technologies Inc said Tuesday the recent rise in the trading volume of its common stock may be due to increased short interest which developed after the price of its common stock rose rapidly during the fourth quarter of 1996.
Recent negative articles about the company may also be a reason, it said, but added it was not aware of any fundamental reason to explain the trading volume increase of its stock.
It said reports have indicated that short interest in its common stock has risen from about 340,000 shares in September 1996 to about 2.9 million shares in January 1997.
It said its average daily volume of shares sold in January 1997 reached over 1.1 million, and at times exceeded two million.

The company's chairman and chief executive officer, Emanuel Pinez, said Centennial remains on track in its plans to broaden product offerings beyond its core personal computer card-based business and bringing contract manufacturing services to its original equipment manufacturing customers.
At the same time, Centennial continues to pursue opportunities and strategic alliances in PC card-based systems and complementary technologies, he said.
